title: Unbounded derived and K-flat tensor calculus for finite clopen module gluing
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $I$ be a finite set, and let $j_i:X_i\hookrightarrow X$ be pairwise disjoint open and closed subschemes whose images cover $X$ [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-closed-immersion]. Use the small pro-etale sites and their fixed universes [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site].

Let $R$ be a sheaf of commutative rings, put $R_i=R|_{X_i}$, and let $r_i$, $G$, and $e_i$ be restriction, the sectionwise product gluing functor, and zero insertion, respectively, of [lem-pur-clopen-ringed-module-gluing]. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], their unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], sheaf tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], and K-flat complexes [def-pc-kflat-complex]. Degreewise restriction induces a triangulated equivalence
$$D(R)\simeq\prod_iD(R_i),\qquad K\longmapsto(r_iK)_i,$$
with quasi-inverse $(K_i)_i\longmapsto\bigoplus_i e_iK_i$. The module insertion and restriction identities remain natural identities on these derived categories, and $H^m(r_iK)\cong r_iH^m(K)$; the $r_i$ jointly detect vanishing and isomorphisms.

There are natural tensor comparisons $r_i(F\otimes_R H)\cong r_iF\otimes_{R_i}r_iH$ and $r_iR\cong R_i$, whose maps on pure tensors are $f\otimes h\mapsto r_if\otimes r_ih$. They preserve the associativity, symmetry and unit constraints. The same comparisons hold for the total tensor complexes, including their differentials. A module is flat, meaning its sheaf tensor functor is exact, if and only if all its components are flat; a complex $P$ is K-flat if and only if all $r_iP$ are K-flat. The induced derived equivalence is symmetric monoidal for the K-flat derived tensor [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent]:
$$r_i(K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}L)\cong r_iK\otimes_{R_i}^{\mathbf L}r_iL.$$
For every morphism $R\to S$ of commutative ring sheaves on this site, it also identifies derived extension of scalars with the component extensions:
$$r_i(K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}S)\cong r_iK\otimes_{R_i}^{\mathbf L}S|_{X_i}.$$
These are natural comparisons on derived objects and morphisms, compatible with the canonical comparison for composites of coefficient ring maps. They include finite coefficient reductions and reductions from the completed ring. The assertions include the empty partition and the zero categories.

Agent finite-product application, old item steps 4-6.

proof.text: Apply the additive exact equivalence $r$ and quasi-inverse $G$ of [lem-pur-clopen-ringed-module-gluing] degreewise, including on differentials and homotopies. The identities $r_iG\cong\operatorname{pr}_i$ and $Gr\cong1$ give an equivalence of complex categories with $\prod_i\mathrm{CoCh}(R_i)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology], $H^m(r_iK)\cong r_iH^m(K)$, naturally in chain maps; likewise for the exact insertion $e_i$. Hence a chain map is a quasi-isomorphism exactly when every restricted chain map is: its cohomology maps are isomorphisms exactly when their restrictions are, by the module equivalence.

source.place: Tag 015F, lemma-right-derived-exact-functor; Tag 05RU, definition-unbounded-derived-category; explicit finite-component application

proof.text: For each $i$, localize degreewise $r_i$ and $e_i$ using [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]. The product $\prod_i Q_{R_i}$ is a localization at componentwise quasi-isomorphisms by [lem-sfb-product-localization]; its index set is finite and each quasi-isomorphism class contains identities. The functor $Q_R G$ on tuples of complexes inverts these arrows by step 1, so [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] gives a functor $G_D:\prod_iD(R_i)\to D(R)$. The degreewise unit and counit descend to natural isomorphisms $G_Dr_D\cong1$ and $r_DG_D\cong1$ by the natural-transformation clause of that same universal property, applied to $Q_R$ and to $\prod_iQ_{R_i}$. Their triangle equations descend because localization is faithful on natural transformations. This proves the derived equivalence on objects and morphisms, without identifying localization morphisms with chain maps.

source.place: Tags 05RU and 015F; agent application of the localization universal property and finite-product localization

proof.text: The exact-functor factorization makes every $r_i$ triangulated. The inverse respects shifts and cone triangles as well: apply the additive $G$ to the degreewise cone matrices, whose entries are differentials, the given map, zero and minus the differential. This gives precisely the cone of the glued map; componentwise cone presentations of a distinguished triangle give such a presentation after gluing. The natural module identities $r_ie_i\cong1$, $r_ie_j=0$ for $i\ne j$, and $\bigoplus_i e_ir_i\cong1$ descend through localization, as in step 2. Thus $G_D((K_i))\cong\bigoplus_i e_iK_i$. Here finite sums may be computed by finite sums of representatives, since kernels and images of a finite direct sum of differentials are the finite direct sums of its kernels and images, and the cone matrices have those same finite sums. Step 1's cohomology comparison also descends. If all components of an object vanish, the inverse equivalence gives the zero object. If every component of a morphism is invertible, apply $G_D$ to the tuple of inverses and conjugate by $G_Dr_D\cong1$ to obtain its inverse. This proves both detection assertions.

source.place: Tag 05RU, definition-unbounded-derived-category; Tag 015F; shift and cone formulas

proof.text: Put $T=G((r_iF\otimes_{R_i}r_iH)_i)$. On sections over $U$, send $(f,h)$ to the tuple $(f|_{U\times_X X_i}\otimes h|_{U\times_X X_i})_i$. This is an $R$-bilinear sheaf map. By [lem-pc-sites-sheaf-tensor-bilinear-universal] it induces $a:F\otimes_RH\to T$. Restricting the universal bilinear map $F\times H\to F\otimes_RH$ gives bilinear maps on every component and hence maps $b_i:r_iF\otimes_{R_i}r_iH\to r_i(F\otimes_RH)$. Glue the $b_i$ and use $Gr\cong1$ to get $b:T\to F\otimes_RH$. The composite $ba$ is the identity because its composite with the universal bilinear map is unchanged. Each component of $ab$ is the identity because it fixes every pure tensor, so $ab=1$ by the module equivalence. This constructs the desired comparison, natural in $F,H$, with its stated pure-tensor formula. The equality $r_iR=R_i$ is the definition of $R_i$. The associator, interchange and unit diagrams agree respectively on $f\otimes h\otimes k$, $f\otimes h$, and $a\otimes f$; their values are the same rebracketed tensor, exchanged tensor and product $af$. Bilinear uniqueness proves the diagrams.

source.place: Tag 0GMW, lemma-sheafification-tensor, and following bilinear universal property in Section 03EK; explicit gluing argument

proof.text: The module equivalence gives $r_i\dashv e_i$: both $\operatorname{Hom}(r_iF,M)$ and $\operatorname{Hom}(F,e_iM)$ are the $i$th component Hom set, all other target components being zero. Therefore [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits] implies that $r_i$ preserves the countable direct sums indexed by $p+q=n$. Apply step 4 on every summand of the total tensor [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. This gives $r_i\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_RQ)\cong\operatorname{Tot}(r_iP\otimes_{R_i}r_iQ)$. It commutes with the differential: on the $(p,q)$ summand both composites send $x\otimes y$ to $r_i(dx)\otimes r_iy+(-1)^p r_ix\otimes r_i(dy)$. Naturality on chain maps follows from the same summand formula. All sums used are small in the fixed module universe.

source.place: Tag 0FPQ, tensor complexes; signed direct-sum totalization; explicit component calculation

proof.text: Flatness is exactness of the tensor functor [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. If every $r_iF$ is flat, restrict any short exact sequence, tensor each restricted sequence, use step 4, and detect exactness by [lem-pur-clopen-ringed-module-gluing]; this proves that $F$ is flat. Conversely, for a short exact sequence on $X_i$, insert it by the exact $e_i$, tensor by flat $F$, and restrict by exact $r_i$. Step 4 and $r_ie_i\cong1$ identify the result with tensoring the original sequence by $r_iF$. Thus $r_iF$ is flat. No exactness of a section functor or stalk criterion is used.

source.place: Flatness by exact sheaf tensor, and Section 03EK; elementary application to component exact sequences

proof.text: Use the acyclic-test definition [def-pc-kflat-complex]. If all $r_iP$ are K-flat and $A$ is acyclic, step 1 makes all $r_iA$ acyclic. Step 5 identifies the restrictions of $\operatorname{Tot}(A\otimes_RP)$ with acyclic complexes $\operatorname{Tot}(r_iA\otimes_{R_i}r_iP)$; step 1 detects acyclicity, proving $P$ K-flat. Conversely, let $P$ be K-flat and let $B$ be an arbitrary acyclic $R_i$-complex. The exact $e_i$ makes $e_iB$ acyclic. Restrict the acyclic $\operatorname{Tot}(e_iB\otimes_RP)$ and use step 5 and $r_ie_i\cong1$ to obtain acyclicity of $\operatorname{Tot}(B\otimes_{R_i}r_iP)$. This is K-flatness of $r_iP$, without a boundedness or flat-term hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 06YN, definition-K-flat; direct use of the acyclic-test definition

proof.text: Choose K-flat resolutions $P\to K$ and $Q\to L$ with flat terms using [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. By steps 1, 6 and 7 their restrictions are K-flat resolutions with flat terms. The K-flat model comparisons of [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] identify the isomorphism of step 5 with $r_i(K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}L)\cong r_iK\otimes_{R_i}^{\mathbf L}r_iL$. To obtain a comparison of functors, first use step 5 as a natural transformation on the homotopy category of K-flat flat-term complexes in both variables. That category localized at its quasi-isomorphisms is equivalent to $D(R)$, and its component counterpart is equivalent to $D(R_i)$, by the same descent node. Its natural-transformation clause extends the comparison and its inverse uniquely to the derived categories. Consequently the displayed isomorphism is natural for every derived morphism and independent of resolutions.

source.place: Tags 06YS, lemma-K-flat-resolution; 0G7D, lemma-factor-through-K-flat; 06YU, definition-derived-tor; normalized comparison on resolutions

proof.text: The symmetric monoidal structures on these derived categories have unit $R[0]$ and $R_i[0]$, and their constraints are induced from total tensors of K-flat representatives, with braiding $x\otimes y\mapsto(-1)^{pq}y\otimes x$, by [lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal]. Its small-site hypothesis holds in the fixed universes. On such representatives, step 4 preserves ordinary associators and multiplication, and step 5 preserves the degree $(p,q)$ summands and their signs. Thus the derived associativity and both unit compatibility diagrams agree on all pure triple tensors and ring-times-section generators; the symmetry diagram agrees because $r_i((-1)^{pq}y\otimes x)=(-1)^{pq}r_iy\otimes r_ix$. The constraints in the cited node are precisely induced by these formulas. By the equivalence of localized K-flat models in [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent], every tuple of derived objects has such representatives, and naturality identifies these equalities with the diagrams for arbitrary derived objects. This proves the symmetric monoidal assertion for the prescribed comparisons, rather than choosing a transported monoidal structure.

source.place: Tags 0FPQ and 0FPT, tensor constraints and derived tensor; Koszul sign and unit formulas

proof.text: For $R\to S$, apply the same gluing to $S$-modules and write $S_i=r_iS$. On a K-flat flat-term $R$-complex $P$, step 4 gives an $S_i$-linear chain isomorphism $r_i(P\otimes_RS)\cong r_iP\otimes_{R_i}S_i$, sending $p\otimes s$ to $r_ip\otimes r_is$. By [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], these complexes compute derived extension of scalars, since $P$ and $r_iP$ are K-flat. This chain comparison is natural on K-flat models and sends inverted arrows to isomorphisms by clause (1) of that node. Descend it and its inverse along the equivalence of K-flat flat-term models with $D(R)$ in [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent], using the natural-transformation clause of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property]. It follows that the scalar comparison is $S_i$-linear, natural for arbitrary derived morphisms and independent of every resolution choice; it is not just the underlying $R_i$-module comparison.

source.place: Tags 06YT, lemma-derived-tor-quasi-isomorphism-other-side, and 06YY, lemma-derived-base-change, for the identity site and a coefficient ring map

proof.text: For composable maps $R\to S\xrightarrow{\psi}T$, choose a K-flat flat-term $R$-resolution $P$. The cancellation isomorphism of [lem-sfb-scalar-tensor-cancellation-independent] identifies, after exact scalar restriction, $\operatorname{Tot}(A\otimes_S(P\otimes_RS))$ with $\operatorname{Tot}(\operatorname{Res}A\otimes_RP)$ for every acyclic $S$-complex $A$. Exact scalar restriction and its detection of zero cohomology follow directly from unchanged underlying sheaves and differentials; the same cancellation degreewise shows that $P^n\otimes_RS$ is flat over $S$ because $P^n$ is flat over $R$. Thus $P\otimes_RS$ is K-flat with flat terms; by steps 1, 6, 7 and 10, $r_iP$ is a K-flat flat-term resolution of $r_iK$ over $R_i$ and $r_i(P\otimes_RS)\cong r_iP\otimes_{R_i}S_i$ is K-flat with flat terms over $S_i$. By [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] the composite derived extension is computed by $(P\otimes_RS)\otimes_ST$. The canonical comparison for the composite is the natural isomorphism $(-\otimes^{\mathbf L}_RS)\otimes^{\mathbf L}_ST\cong-\otimes^{\mathbf L}_RT$ of [lem-sfb-successive-derived-quotient-normalization], whose small-site hypothesis holds in the fixed universes. By that statement it is represented on the K-flat flat-term representative $P$ by $(p\otimes s)\otimes t\mapsto p\otimes\psi(s)t$. On $X_i$, for $R_i\to S_i\xrightarrow{\psi_i}T_i$ and $r_iP$, it is represented by the same formula with $\psi_i$. Compose step 10 for $R\to S$ on $P$, for $\psi$ on $P\otimes_RS$, and for $R\to T$ on $P$. Both paths of the composition square then send $(p\otimes s)\otimes t$ to $r_ip\otimes\psi_i(r_is)r_it$, so the square commutes on representatives. Descent from K-flat models as in step 10 makes it commute on derived objects and morphisms. For the identity coefficient map the comparison of step 10 is $r_ip\otimes a\mapsto a\,r_ip$ under $r_iP\otimes_{R_i}R_i\cong r_iP$, so identity comparisons are preserved.

source.place: Tag 05V4, lemma-flat-change-of-rings, tensor cancellation; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 0D6D, lemma-derived-pullback-composition; explicit scalar compositor calculation

proof.text: For finite quotient coefficient maps and maps from the completed integral coefficient ring [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients], step 10 applies without requiring flatness of the quotient; the coefficient identifications and transition maps are those supplied by [lem-pur-clopen-ringed-module-gluing], and step 11 proves their compatibility under composition. Finally, an empty component has the zero module category by the gluing node, hence only zero complexes and a derived category equivalent to the category with one object and one arrow. If $I$ is empty, its images cover only $X=\varnothing$, so both sides are these zero categories; all maps and diagrams above are then unique, flatness and K-flatness hold for their sole object, and the tensor unit is zero. This also handles zero coefficient sheaves on any component.

source.place: Tag 05RU; specialization to zero module categories; coefficient maps from the gluing statement
